prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity 16:9 DESKTOP WEBSITE UI MOCKUP for a portfolio home page, shown edge-to-edge at a 1440 × 810 viewport; no browser frame, no device frame.
Primary request: Design “The Remembered Street,” an interactive guided-scroll portfolio for Nazar Falach. This must unmistakably read as a finished website interface over a navigable spatial district, not a standalone landscape, poster, cover, or concept-art scene.

Interface structure and hierarchy:
- Roughly the upper half of the viewport is a broad, quiet high-blue sky, giving breathing room and strong visual hierarchy.
- The lower half is one continuous daylight Dreamcore neighborhood with rolling meadow turf and sparse pastel clapboard buildings.
- A pale S-curved sidewalk enters from the lower-right corner, passes the active project in the near foreground, and recedes through all six landmarks toward a very small white water tower at the horizon. The path implies guided vertical scroll.
- Anchor the lower-left foreground with a simple off-white civic street-sign assembly carrying Nazar’s identity. It is a physical sign integrated into the district, large and highly readable, not a floating card.
- The active first landmark is PulseGuard: a lonely peach-and-off-white watch-house in the near middle-right, with exactly three warm porch lamps and one small attached off-white evidence panel. Make it the clear current stop without sci-fi styling.
- Let five clearly different landmark silhouettes recede along the route: CoLab is two small houses physically joined by one shared bridge/room; Foundation is a compact civic publishing house with a notice-board facade; Prime Leather Repair is a split workshop whose two halves are visibly stitched/repaired together; BookShelf is a little house whose roofline resembles a bookshelf; Local LLM Fine-Tuning is a modest old school computer room with a row of softly glowing CRT windows. These must remain buildings/places within one coherent neighborhood, not UI cards.
- A disciplined, slim off-white street-directory navigation rail spans the bottom edge as real persistent website chrome. Six evenly paced stops, a thin route line, a clear active PulseGuard state, restrained navy type, no numbered step badges, no rounded cards.
- Put a small unobtrusive “Contact” text action at the top-right edge with a precise underline/route tick.
- Keep all other interface chrome extremely quiet. No generic navbar, hero card, dashboard, glass panels, or grids.

Exact text, verbatim and correctly spelled. Render only these legible words; do not invent any other copy, numbers, labels, URLs, metrics, or claims:
“Nazar Falach”
“Full-stack engineer · Poland”
“Six places. One remembered street.”
“PulseGuard”
“CoLab”
“Foundation”
“Prime Leather Repair”
“BookShelf”
“Local LLM Fine-Tuning”
“Contact”
The street-sign identity shows the first three lines. The bottom directory contains the six project stop names exactly once each. “PulseGuard” may also appear once on its small active evidence panel. “Contact” appears once at top right. Use restrained humanist civic sans-serif lettering, clean and readable.

Controlled surrealism, secondary to usability: the street sign casts a long shadow in the physically wrong direction; one freestanding white door floats slightly above the distant meadow; two small clouds repeat with impossible identical silhouettes; one far segment of the sidewalk makes a subtle impossible loop before continuing. Keep these discoveries quiet, charming, and strange—never horror.

Style/medium: polished production-grade website art direction; stylized low-poly 3D environment with believable perspective and designed UI overlay; pastel clapboard architecture, low-poly turf, matte civic paint, slightly soft 1990s analog color bleed and fine film grain. Dreamlike but professionally art-directed.
Color palette: high sky blue dominant, saturated meadow green, lavender atmospheric haze, peach siding, off-white signs, restrained navy interface ink, tiny warm amber lamps.
Lighting/mood: clear empty daylight, sunny nostalgic suburban stillness, comforting with a slight uncanny undertone. No people.
Composition safeguards: keep every required interface label within safe margins; bottom directory must be fully visible and readable; the active PulseGuard landmark must not collide with the identity sign; retain generous quiet sky; make the scene feel scrollable through route alignment and active-stop UI.
Avoid: observatory, dome, vivarium, conservatory, sci-fi, futuristic architecture, neon, chrome, glass HUD, generic cards, floating dashboard panels, black background, night, horror, gore, eyes, mushrooms, characters, vehicles, watermark, logos, browser chrome, fake claims, extra text, misspelled text, poster composition.
